# @vllnt/convex-metering

> Usage metering as a Convex component: idempotent usage events rolled up per billing period, with atomic limits, period close and signed corrections.

Install `@vllnt/convex-metering` (unreleased builds from `main` use the `canary` dist-tag). Peer
dependency `convex@^1.45.0`; optional peer `react >=18` for the `./react` hooks; Node.js `>=20`
(`engines.node`; `convex` 1.51 needs `>=22`). ES modules only. Mount it with
`app.use(metering)` from `@vllnt/convex-metering/convex.config` and call it through
`new Metering(components.metering)` from host mutations and queries. Mutations: `defineMeter`,
`record`, `recordWithLimit`, `adjust`, `closePeriod`, `reset`, `eraseSubject`, `pruneRecords`,
`pruneSeen`. Queries: `getMeter`, `listMeters`, `usage`, `listUsage`, `listSubjectUsage`, `verify`.
A meter has an aggregation (`sum` adds, `max` keeps the peak, `last` keeps the latest), locked once
it has a rollup (`AGGREGATION_LOCKED`). Each `(meter, subjectRef, period)` has one rollup
`{ value, count, closed }`; `period` is an opaque host string (no date parsing). `idempotencyKey`
works on `sum` meters only, is scoped to `(scope, meter)` (not subject or period), lives in a `seen`
table that survives `reset`, `eraseSubject` and `pruneRecords`, and is removed only by `pruneSeen`.
`recordWithLimit` records only when the projected rollup is `<= limit`, else returns
`limit_exceeded`. `adjust` posts a signed delta to a `sum` meter, never below zero.
`closePeriod` makes later writes to that period throw `PERIOD_CLOSED` (checked before the duplicate
check). `verify` re-folds the surviving records and compares values only. Client defaults:
`defaultScope: "global"`, `defaultPeriod: "all"`; meter defaults `aggregation: "sum"`, `unit: ""`.
Cleanup batches default to 200, integer 1..500 (`INVALID_BATCH`); they return the first pass's count
and reschedule while full. `pruneRecords` and `pruneSeen` span every scope. List queries and
`verify` are not paginated; `listUsage` is sorted by period, `listMeters` and `listSubjectUsage`
return creation order. Errors are `ConvexError` with `data.code`. `defineMeter`, `record`,
`recordWithLimit` and `adjust` reject an empty string argument or one longer than 256 UTF-16 code
units (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`); queries and `closePeriod`, `reset`, `eraseSubject`, `pruneRecords`,
`pruneSeen` are not capped, so older longer rows stay readable and erasable, but recording,
adjusting or redefining (`defineMeter`) them throws. The host owns auth,
`subjectRef`, `period`, pricing and retention; scopes are not authorization.

## When to use

- Use it when you bill or report usage per subject and period and a retried event must not be
  counted twice.
- Use it when a usage cap must be checked and recorded in one transaction, or a billed period must
  be frozen and corrected with an audit trail.
- Do not use it for allowances that reset on a schedule: use `@vllnt/convex-quota`. Do not use it
  for prepaid balances: use `@vllnt/convex-wallet`. Do not use it to throttle requests per time
  window: use a rate limiter such as `@convex-dev/rate-limiter`.

## For coding agents

The docs are bundled in the npm package at `node_modules/@vllnt/convex-metering/docs/` and match the
installed version. Read them, and the bundled `src/`, before writing code. The links below to `./`
paths are files inside the installed package.

- [README](./README.md): Install, quick start, common tasks, limits
